paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence “Living in an increasingly competitive world, college students should better prepare themselves to confront various challenges.” You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：对于这一部分，你有 30 分钟的时间写一篇文章，开头是“生活在竞争日益激烈的世界中，大学生应该更好地准备自己应对各种挑战”。您可以发表评论、引用示例或利用您的个人经历来完善您的论文。你应该写至少150字但不超过200字。

paragraphs.sourceText: You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您应该复制论文开头引号中给出的句子。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，有一段有十个空格。您需要从文章后面的单词库中给出的选项列表中为每个空白选择一个单词。在做出选择之前仔细阅读该段落。银行中的每个选择都由一个字母标识。请在答题卡 2 上的每个项目上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。您不得多次使用银行中的任何单词。

paragraphs.sourceText: It’s best to think of an accent as a distinct, systematic and rule-governed way of speaking. Accent is not a 26 for dialect, but it’s related. Dialect is an umbrella term for the way a community pronounces words, creates words, and orders words; accent refers to that first part only.
paragraphs.translationZh: 最好将口音视为一种独特的、系统的、受规则约束的说话方式。口音不是方言的同义词，但它是相关的。方言是社区发音、创造单词和排序单词方式的总称；重音仅指第一部分。

paragraphs.sourceText: Many 27 presume that there is a single standard way of speaking in each country, with one single standard accent, and that this perceived standard is 28 the best form of speech, but linguists (语言学家) often point out that the concept of a standard accent is better understood as an ideal rather than a 29 . In other words, no one speaks “standard English”; rather, it is an imagined way of using language that exists only in grammar and style books.
paragraphs.translationZh: 许多外行人认为每个国家都有一种标准的说话方式，有一种标准口音，并且这种感知的标准本质上是最好的语言形式，但语言学家（语言学家）经常指出，标准口音的概念最好被理解为一种理想而不是现实。换句话说，没有人会说“标准英语”；相反，它是一种想象的使用语言的方式，只存在于语法和文体书籍中。

paragraphs.sourceText: One reason linguists agree there is no one true standard is that, through the years, there have been 30 supposed standards, depending on time and place. The standard for English in British newsreels (新闻片) from the 1950s, for example, differs greatly from the standard found on American national news broadcasts today. In fact, there has never been a single standard that’s been fully agreed upon — and broadcast outlets across the 31 have never consistently held to those standards anyway.
paragraphs.translationZh: 语言学家一致认为没有一个真正的标准的原因之一是，多年来，根据时间和地点的不同，存在多种假定的标准。例如，20 世纪 50 年代英国新闻片的英语标准与当今美国国家新闻广播的英语标准有很大不同。事实上，从来没有一个标准得到完全认可，而且各个领域的广播机构也从未始终如一地遵守这些标准。

paragraphs.sourceText: Even so, this idea of a standard accent is 32 and many workplace and educational environments perpetuate the idea that accents that 33 from the current standard are less appropriate, or even inappropriate. Scholars have found that southern US accent features are more accepted in 34 such as government, law and service-oriented workplaces, but less accepted in the technology sector. The acceptability of nonstandard accents may 35 with differences in class and culture, with newer or higher prestige industries expecting more standard speech in the workplace.
paragraphs.translationZh: 即便如此，这种标准口音的想法仍然具有影响力，许多工作场所和教育环境延续了这样的观念：偏离当前标准的口音不太合适，甚至不合适。学者们发现，美国南部口音特征在政府、法律和服务型工作场所等领域更容易被接受，但在科技领域则不太被接受。非标准口音的可接受性可能与阶层和文化的差异有关，较新或较高声望的行业期望在工作场所有更多标准的言语。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: The History and Meaning of Colored Traffic Lights
paragraphs.translationZh: 彩色交通灯的历史和意义

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Timed traffic lights are set according to schedules that are supposed to coordinate with peak traffic hours. Cities need to monitor and update signal light time schedules at least every two years to keep these systems effective. In Los Angeles, California, an ambitious project to go a step further and synchronize (使同步) every red light in Los Angeles cost over 400 million dollars. Ask a resident of the city and they are likely to agree that saving time on the road is well worth it. If implemented nationwide, synchronization could shave 10% off traffic congestion (堵塞) and 20% off air pollution. Congestion costs time, money, and lives. Big data can help improve how millions of people safely share the road. However, none of this would be possible without the traffic light!
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 定时交通灯是根据与高峰交通时间协调的时间表设置的。城市需要至少每两年监控和更新信号灯时间表，以保持这些系统的有效性。在加利福尼亚州洛杉矶，一个雄心勃勃的项目耗资超过 4 亿美元，旨在进一步同步洛杉矶的每个红灯。如果询问该市的居民，他们可能会同意节省路上的时间是非常值得的。如果在全国范围内实施，同步可以减少 10% 的交通拥堵和 20% 的空气污染。拥堵会耗费时间、金钱和生命。大数据可以帮助改善数百万人安全共享道路的方式。然而，如果没有红绿灯，这一切都是不可能的！

paragraphs.sourceText: B) The first traffic light was invented in London in the 1860’s, but it was hardly recognizable — or effective. It had been adapted from the railroad signal system by a railway manager, John Peak Knight, in 1868. The railroads used red gas lights at night to signal stops and green gas lights during the daytime. Knight installed a similar gas light, semaphore (臂板信号) system near London’s Westminster Bridge in December of 1868.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 第一个交通信号灯于 1860 年代在伦敦发明，但它几乎难以辨认，也难以发挥作用。它是由铁路经理约翰·皮克·奈特 (John Peak Knight) 于 1868 年根据铁路信号系统改编而成。铁路在夜间使用红色煤气灯来指示车站，在白天使用绿色煤气灯。 1868 年 12 月，奈特在伦敦威斯敏斯特桥附近安装了类似的煤气灯、信号机 (臂板信号) 系统。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) The life of the first traffic light signal was short-lived. A gas leak caused one of the signal lights to explode on its police officer operator within a month of being installed.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 第一个交通灯信号的寿命很短。在安装后一个月内，煤气泄漏导致其中一个信号灯在警务操作员身上爆炸。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) Automating traffic signals stalled after the London incident. Forty years passed before cars crowding city streets urged the development of traffic lights in the United States. London would not see another traffic light until 1929.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 伦敦事件后，自动化交通信号陷入停滞。四十年过去了，挤满城市街道的汽车促使美国交通信号灯的发展。直到 1929 年，伦敦才出现了另一个红绿灯。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) The United States is a car culture like no other country. Unlike most European cities that started urban planning when horses were high-tech, many cities in the United States were designed around urban sprawl, suburban tracts, and motor cars.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 美国的汽车文化与其他国家不同。与大多数欧洲城市在马匹还是高科技时就开始城市规划不同，美国的许多城市都是围绕城市扩张、郊区和机动车而设计的。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) As traffic and cities grew, so did the race to solve growing traffic problems. The first traffic signals were semaphores. Semaphores are towers with moving arms signaling for traffic to stop or go. They could be manual or automatic. There was no consistent design. Various models were invented and put into place in cities as the need arose.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 随着交通和城市的发展，解决日益严重的交通问题的竞赛也在加剧。第一个交通信号是信号量。信号灯是带有移动臂的塔，向交通发出停止或通行的信号。它们可以是手动的或自动的。没有一致的设计。随着需要的出现，各种模型被发明并在城市中应用。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) In 1912, Lester Wire was a police officer exhausted by traffic at Main Street and 200 South. He developed a manually switched stop light. The four-sided box, raised on a ten-foot pole, looked like a birdhouse and was operated manually by an officer. The officer would flip a switch to change between the dipped red and green lights.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 1912 年，莱斯特·威尔 (Lester Wire) 是一名警察，因主街和南 200 号的交通堵塞而疲惫不堪。他开发了一种手动开关刹车灯。这个四边形的盒子立在一根十英尺长的杆子上，看起来像一个鸟舍，由一名军官手动操作。警官会扳动开关，在微弱的红灯和绿灯之间切换。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Like the 1910 semaphore, the first electric signal used words. However, the words were no longer written on arms that raised and fell. The words “stop” or “move” were on lights. The posts lit up on each of four corner-posts around an intersection (十字路口). It was not automated, though. A booth with an operator was required to flip the switches.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 就像 1910 年的信号量一样，第一个电信号使用了文字。不过，举起落下的手臂上，已经不再写着这几个字了。灯光上写着“停止”或“移动”。十字路口周围的四个角柱上的每个柱子都亮起来。但它不是自动化的。需要一个配备操作员的摊位来翻转开关。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) The system allowed police officers to move from the middle of the street to a corner. From that vantage (有利地位), an officer could oversee the crowd. If an emergency vehicle came, the officer could flip a switch and clear the intersection by triggering all red lights. The emergency vehicle could now pass effortlessly. Finally, in San Francisco the first red and green electric light system that could be operated automatically (or manually) was introduced in 1917.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 该系统允许警察从街道中间移动到街角。从有利位置来看，军官可以监督人群。如果有紧急车辆到来，警察可以打开开关并触发所有红灯以清除十字路口。紧急车辆现在可以毫不费力地通过了。最后，旧金山于 1917 年推出了第一个可以自动（或手动）操作的红绿电灯系统。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) In 1920, the first three-color light system was introduced in Detroit — also known as Motor City, USA. The evolution of traffic light signals could not have a more appropriate context than Motor City. Ford Motor Company was founded in Detroit in 1903 (and other motor companies followed). Ford made cars affordable for more common people, rather than the wealthy, by creating larger scale factory production.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 1920 年，第一个三色灯光系统在美国底特律（又称汽车城）推出。交通灯信号的演变没有比汽车城更合适的背景了。福特汽车公司于 1903 年在底特律成立（随后其他汽车公司也纷纷效仿）。福特通过建立更大规模的工厂生产，让更多普通人而不是富人买得起汽车。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Stop and go were insufficient for the new volumes of cars zooming through intersections. Streets were full of new numbers of cars in addition to delivery wagons, bustling crowds, bicycles, horse-drawn carriages, and street cars. The introduction of the cautionary yellow light helped increase driver safety, decreasing accidents that come from running red lights.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 停车和走动对于新数量的汽车在十字路口快速行驶来说是不够的。街道上除了货车、熙熙攘攘的人群、自行车、马车和街车外，还停满了新的汽车。警示性黄灯的引入有助于提高驾驶员的安全性，减少闯红灯造成的事故。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Stop lights were incredibly important in chaotic city streets. Crosswalks weren’t even introduced until 1951. The first pedestrian fatality in the United States was in 1899.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 红绿灯在混乱的城市街道上非常重要。人行横道直到 1951 年才被引入。美国第一起行人死亡事件发生在 1899 年。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) The development of the modern traffic light may have started in London, but it grew up in the United States. In Cleveland, an African-American inventor named Garrett Morgan came up with an affordable, patented traffic signal. The yellow light made intersections safer than the old stop and go system. The new design was inexpensive enough that it allowed the installation of a lot more lights.
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 现代交通信号灯的发展可能始于伦敦，但它是在美国发展起来的。在克利夫兰，一位名叫加勒特摩根的非裔美国发明家发明了一种价格实惠的专利交通信号灯。黄灯使十字路口比旧的走走停停系统更安全。新设计足够便宜，可以安装更多的灯。

paragraphs.sourceText: N) Morgan sold the patent to General Electric — and the spread of the traffic light was green lighted. Green means go. It is that simple, but it’s still best to check both ways for oncoming traffic that may not be paying attention or is running the light. Yellow means slow down and prepare to stop. It does not mean full-throttle (全速) ahead. While you may get away with gunning it into the intersection, running a yellow can lead to tickets and dangerous accidents. Red lights are a clear and consistent warning to stop. Even where right turns are allowed on red lights, you must come to a complete stop before turning right. You must also yield to any through traffic, which has the right of way. In most states and cities, you can take a right on red unless otherwise indicated. New York City does not allow a right on red.
paragraphs.translationZh: N）摩根将专利卖给了通用电气——红绿灯的普及就亮了绿灯。绿色意味着走。就是这么简单，但最好还是检查两条路是否有迎面驶来的车辆，这些车辆可能没有注意或闯红灯。黄色表示减速并准备停车。这并不意味着全速前进。虽然你可能会在路口开枪逃脱，但闯黄灯可能会导致罚单和危险事故。红灯是明确且一致的停车警告。即使在红灯时允许右转的地方，您也必须完全停车后才能右转。您还必须给任何有通行权的直行车辆让行。在大多数州和城市，除非另有说明，您可以在红灯处右转。纽约市不允许红灯右转。

paragraphs.sourceText: O) Red arrows mean you cannot turn right on a red in most states. The green arrow, in these cases, is the only time you can make the turn. However, you can take a right on a red arrow after a full stop in the states of Illinois, Kansas, Louisiana, Maryland, Michigan, New Hampshire, North Dakota, Oregon, South Carolina, Utah, Washington State and Wyoming. P. Flashing Red is the same as a stop sign, generally used at four-way intersections where there is minimal traffic. When arriving at a flashing red light, make a full and complete stop. Flashing Red Arrows similarly mean to stop and then proceed to take the turn. Flashing Yellow lights mean yield or signal caution, like outside of a fire station. There are no all-direction flashing yellow lights, since it is prohibited in the United States. If you have a flashing yellow light, you are to yield to oncoming traffic. Q. Flashing Yellow Arrows are part of a four-signal traffic light. These are used in some states after a protected green turn signal, or arrow, but before a steady yellow arrow. When a flashing yellow arrow is shown, you can take the turn after yielding to pedestrians and traffic. Steady Yellow Arrows maintain the normal yellow light caution in three-light signals, meaning to stop or prepare to stop. In a four-signal system that has a flashing yellow arrow, the steady yellow arrow is a signal that the yield period is ending. The red arrow is about to start. Vehicles should stop if safely possible. Traffic tickets are possible for running a steady yellow arrow. R. Traffic light meaning is fairly consistent across the board with various deviations. Green means it’s safe to proceed (though you should still exercise caution). Yellow means caution and yield. Red means danger and stop. Always drive defensively and obey traffic signals.
paragraphs.translationZh: O) 红色箭头表示在大多数州您不能在红灯处右转。在这些情况下，绿色箭头是您可以转弯的唯一时间。但是，在伊利诺伊州、堪萨斯州、路易斯安那州、马里兰州、密歇根州、新罕布什尔州、北达科他州、俄勒冈州、南卡罗来纳州、犹他州、华盛顿州和怀俄明州，您可以在完全停止后沿红色箭头右转。 P. 闪烁红灯与停车标志相同，通常用于交通量最少的四向路口。当到达闪烁的红灯时，完全停车。闪烁的红色箭头同样表示停止然后继续转弯。闪烁的黄灯表示让行或发出警告信号，例如在消防站外。没有全方位闪烁的黄灯，因为在美国是禁止的。如果黄灯闪烁，则应礼让迎面驶来的车辆。问：闪烁的黄色箭头是四信号交通灯的一部分。在某些州，它们在受保护的绿色转向灯或箭头之后、稳定的黄色箭头之前使用。当显示闪烁的黄色箭头时，您可以在避让行人和交通后转弯。稳定的黄色箭头保持三灯信号中正常的黄灯警告，意味着停止或准备停止。在具有闪烁黄色箭头的四信号系统中，稳定的黄色箭头表示收益期即将结束。红色箭头即将开始。如果安全的话，车辆应该停下来。运行稳定的黄色箭头可能会收到交通罚单。 R. 交通信号灯的含义总体上相当一致，但存在一些偏差。绿色意味着可以安全地继续（尽管您仍应谨慎行事）。黄色意味着谨慎和屈服。红色意味着危险和停止。始终以防御性驾驶并遵守交通信号。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Upon seeing a flashing yellow arrow, a driver should let pedestrians and traffic pass first before taking the turn.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 司机看到闪烁的黄色箭头时，应先让行人和车辆通过，然后再转弯。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. The red and green automatic traffic light system originated in an American city.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37、红绿自动交通灯系统起源于美国的一座城市。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. Residents of an American city tend to share the opinion that time saved on the road justifies the cost of upgrading its traffic light system.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 美国城市的居民倾向于认为，节省的路上时间证明升级交通灯系统的成本是合理的。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. Mass production of cars made it possible for ordinary people to buy them.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39.汽车的大规模生产使普通人能够购买汽车。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. What a traffic light means is almost the same everywhere despite some variations.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 尽管存在一些差异，但交通信号灯的含义在任何地方几乎都是相同的。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Pedestrian crossings came into being only in the mid-twentieth century.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 行人过路处直到二十世纪中叶才出现。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. People raced to address increasing traffic problems along with the expansion of cities and traffic.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 随着城市和交通的扩张，人们竞相解决日益严重的交通问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. When the warning yellow light was introduced, driving became safer and traffic accidents reduced.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 引入黄灯警告后，驾驶变得更加安全，交通事故也减少了。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. The signal system on the railroad served as the basis for the first traffic light.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 铁路上的信号系统是第一个交通灯的基础。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Even though a green light signals “go”, attention should be paid to traffic on either side in case some driver is being careless or ignoring a red light.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 即使绿灯信号“走”，也应注意两侧的交通，以防某些司机粗心或忽视红灯。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A, B, C and D. You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有 2 段。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A、B、C 和 D。您应该决定最佳选项，并在答题纸 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Mindfulness has been shown to have a number of meaningful health benefits — it can help reduce anxiety and promote healing in those suffering from chronic illness.
paragraphs.translationZh: 正念已被证明具有许多有意义的健康益处——它可以帮助减轻焦虑并促进慢性病患者的康复。

paragraphs.sourceText: The practice is based on an insight first described in ancient Buddhist texts that human beings have the capacity to observe experience without being caught up in it. This means simply that it is possible to observe ourselves having a craving, or a happy thought, or even a scary emotion, without reacting in the moment in a way that amplifies the feeling or sends the mind spiraling off into thinking about old memories or anticipating events.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这种做法基于古代佛教文献中首次描述的洞察力，即人类有能力观察经验而不被困在其中。这仅仅意味着，我们可以观察到自己有一种渴望，或者一种快乐的想法，甚至一种可怕的情绪，而不会在当下做出反应，从而放大这种感觉，或者让大脑陷入回想旧记忆或预期事件的状态。

paragraphs.sourceText: This practice of mindfulness can help calm the mind and the body as we learn not to react to experience with likes and dislikes or judgments of good and bad. It does not make us cold or indifferent but more fully present.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这种正念练习可以帮助我们平静身心，因为我们学会不要对经历做出好恶或好坏判断的反应。它不会让我们变得冷漠或冷漠，而是让我们更加充分地临在。

paragraphs.sourceText: One of the challenges of practicing mindfulness in our contemporary world is that there has been a profound transformation in human attention. The artist Jenny Odell argues that in our “attention economy” human attention has been transformed into a commodity that big corporations buy and sell. This economy rests on a technological revolution of mobile phones and social media that makes it possible for corporations to target our attention with their content at every moment.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在当今世界练习正念的挑战之一是人类注意力发生了深刻的转变。艺术家珍妮·奥德尔认为，在我们的“注意力经济”中，人类的注意力已经转变为大公司买卖的商品。这种经济依赖于移动电话和社交媒体的技术革命，这使得企业能够随时通过其内容吸引我们的注意力。

paragraphs.sourceText: The devices most people use are a perpetual diversion from the present moment. The result is that it can feel as though our ability to focus, and be fully present, has been stolen. But mindfulness can help us resist the attention economy and relish the things that make life special, like being together with those we love.
paragraphs.translationZh: 大多数人使用的设备永远会分散人们当前的注意力。结果是我们感觉好像我们专注和全神贯注的能力被偷走了。但正念可以帮助我们抵制注意力经济，享受那些让生活变得特别的事情，比如和我们所爱的人在一起。

paragraphs.sourceText: Most mindfulness research focuses on the individual benefits of the practice, but some scholars assert that we can not only practice mindfulness for ourselves but also practice it for others. It can help us build stronger, healthier relationships.
paragraphs.translationZh: 大多数正念研究都侧重于练习的个人利益，但一些学者声称，我们不仅可以为自己练习正念，还可以为他人练习。它可以帮助我们建立更牢固、更健康的关系。

paragraphs.sourceText: The sad truth is that living in the attention economy, most of us have become bad listeners. However, just as it is possible to watch ourselves having an experience without reacting, it’s possible to watch another person have an experience without getting tied up in reactivity and judgment.
paragraphs.translationZh: 可悲的事实是，生活在注意力经济中，我们大多数人都成为了糟糕的倾听者。然而，正如我们可以观察自己的经历而不做出反应一样，我们也可以观察另一个人的经历而不被反应和判断所束缚。

paragraphs.sourceText: The gift of mindfulness is a practice of listening with compassion to others describe their experiences. To give this gift means putting away your phone, turning off social media, and setting aside other common distractions. It means practicing being fully present in another person’s presence and listening to them with complete attention without judgment, while resisting the urge to make the interaction about you.
paragraphs.translationZh: 正念的礼物是一种以同情心倾听他人描述他们的经历的练习。送出这份礼物意味着收起手机、关闭社交媒体并抛开其他常见的干扰。这意味着练习完全呈现在另一个人面前，全神贯注地倾听他们而不带任何判断力，同时抵制以你为中心进行互动的冲动。

paragraphs.sourceText: If we judge the value of gifts based on their price, this gift may seem worthless, but in a distracted world, it is a precious one.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果我们根据礼物的价格来判断礼物的价值，这份礼物可能看起来毫无价值，但在一个心烦意乱的世界里，它是一件珍贵的礼物。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: The other day I had to log into a service I hadn’t used before. Since I was a new user, the website decided that it needed to check I wasn’t a robot and so set me a Captcha test to determine whether the user is a person or a machine.
paragraphs.translationZh: 有一天，我不得不登录一个我以前从未使用过的服务。由于我是新用户，网站认为需要检查我不是机器人，因此给我设置了验证码测试来确定用户是人还是机器。

paragraphs.sourceText: I was presented with an image of a roadside scene over which was laid a grid. My “challenge” was to click on each cell in the grid that contained a traffic sign. I did so, a bit irritated. Then I was presented with another image and another grid — also with a request to identify road signs. Like a lamb, I complied, after which the website accepted my input.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我看到了一张路边场景的图像，上面铺设了网格。我的“挑战”是单击网格中包含交通标志的每个单元格。我这样做了，有点生气。然后我看到了另一张图像和另一个网格——还要求识别路标。我像羔羊一样答应了，之后网站接受了我的输入。

paragraphs.sourceText: And then I realised what I had been doing was adding to a dataset for training the machine-learning software that guides self-driving cars. So, to gain access to an automated service that will benefit financially from my input, I first have to do some unpaid labor to help improve the performance of autonomous vehicles.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然后我意识到我一直在做的是添加一个数据集来训练指导自动驾驶汽车的机器学习软件。因此，为了获得能够从我的投入中获得经济利益的自动化服务，我首先必须做一些无偿劳动来帮助提高自动驾驶汽车的性能。

paragraphs.sourceText: Neat, eh? But note also the delicious additional irony that the Captcha is described as an “automated Turing test”. The Turing test was conceived, you may recall, as a way of enabling humans to determine whether a machine could respond in such a way that one couldn’t tell whether it was a human or a robot. So we have wandered into a world in which machines make us do tricks to prove that we are humans!
paragraphs.translationZh: 整洁，嗯？但还要注意一个有趣的额外讽刺，验证码被描述为“自动图灵测试”。您可能还记得，图灵测试的构想是一种使人类能够确定机器是否能够以无法区分它是人类还是机器人的方式做出响应的方式。所以我们已经进入了一个机器让我们做一些戏法来证明我们是人类的世界！

paragraphs.sourceText: The strangest aspect of this unparalleled shift is how under-discussed it has been. The metaphor of the boiling frog comes to mind. Have we become so subtly conditioned by digital technology that we don’t see what’s been happening to us? Have we been conditioned to accept a world governed by “smart” tech, trading convenience to the point where we become a bit like machines ourselves?
paragraphs.translationZh: 这种前所未有的转变最奇怪的一点是，它的讨论却很少。我想到了温水煮青蛙的比喻。我们是否已变得如此微妙地受到数字技术的影响，以至于我们看不到发生在我们身上的事情？我们是否已经习惯于接受一个由“智能”技术统治的世界，牺牲便利，以至于我们自己变得有点像机器？

paragraphs.sourceText: In a recent startling and thoughtful book, two scholars — Brett Frischmann, a law professor, and Evan Selinger, a philosopher — argue that the answer to that question is “yes”.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在最近一本令人震惊且深思熟虑的书中，两位学者——法学教授布雷特·弗里施曼和哲学家埃文·塞林格——认为这个问题的答案是“是”。

paragraphs.sourceText: And they’re right. There’s nothing technophobic (技术恐惧的) about that. We shape our tools and then our tools shape us. Technology is supposed to provide tools that serve human ends. But, as the machine-learning Captcha demonstrates, a significant proportion of digital tech now sees (and uses) humans as means to ends that are not ours. In the process, they reduce us to the status of cheery rats running on treadmills (踏车) designed by people who do not have our interests at heart. So back to the frog metaphor. Are we smart enough to jump out before it’s too late? You don’t even have to Google it to know the answer.
paragraphs.translationZh: 他们是对的。这并没有什么技术恐惧的。我们塑造我们的工具，然后我们的工具塑造我们。技术应该提供服务于人类目的的工具。但是，正如机器学习验证码所表明的那样，很大一部分数字技术现在将人类视为（并使用）人类作为达到不属于我们的目的的手段。在这个过程中，他们把我们变成了在跑步机上奔跑的快乐老鼠，而跑步机的设计者并不关心我们的利益。回到青蛙的比喻。我们是否足够聪明，能够在为时已晚之前跳出来？你甚至不需要谷歌就能知道答案。
